proposal.name: Retry failed plumbing builds by building again

issue_plan.name: Retry failed plumbing builds by building again
issue_plan.summary: A retry after a plumbing build fails in the factory's own run will rebuild the same ratified plan, close its failed draft pull request and open a replacement; a retry after CI fails will still watch the existing pull request. This needs two modeled prerequisites: the issue protocol currently permits only watching when a failed build has a pull request, and the recovery model permits only one pull request per ratification. The final plumbing issue connects those changes, tests all three build-failure cases and CI retries, and makes the posts, dashboard cards, SPEC.md and README describe the actual action. The new rebuild and replacement rules need decisions recorded through the decision tooling by whoever merges the changes; existing decisions do not authorize changing pinned statements without the modeled amendment's ratification.

issues.title: Allow an explicit rebuild retry in the issue protocol
issues.body:
A plumbing build can fail because its agent stopped, its tests failed or its review asked for changes, yet leave a draft pull request. Issue #263 requires a writer's retry in that state to build the already-ratified plan again and replace the failed draft, while a CI-failure retry keeps watching its existing pull request. The current factory/protocol model cannot authorize that rebuild: Retry sends every failed state with a head to pr_open, and Build requires ratified. This issue supplies the protocol prerequisite; later issues supply recovery and plumbing.

Project: factory/protocol

Add an explicit modeled rebuild-retry operation, with no new user command. It is permitted only for a director and a failed own-run build with a pull request, represented by failure=gate and a nonempty head. It returns the issue to ratified, clears the failure and resets stopped-build counting. It preserves the proposal, ratification, amendment and base-lock identities, with no new draft or ratification. It retires the previous active head and its associated gate, PR lock, scope and merge state, so neither the previous draft nor its CI result can stand for the next build. A subsequent stopped build must still satisfy StoppedHasNoPullRequest, and a subsequent successful build must require CI at its own current head before merging.

Keep existing Retry available with its current meaning for existing callers, including stopped builds without a PR, CI failures, unmergeable PRs and modeled-project builds. The protocol has no plumbing-kind field: adding a distinct permitted rebuild step lets the later plumbing adapter select it for a failed plumbing build without changing modeled-project retry policy. Refuse the new operation for CI or merge failures, states other than failed, failures without a PR, nonwriters and bots, without changing state. Do not obtain permission by omitting the real source head from the adapter's view, or describe factory replacement as someone else's OthersClose action.

Amend the project's statements through the modeled proposal and ratification workflow, then update the model, Go implementation and contracts, and explorer. Preserve the State/constants/Successors interface used by the watcher, and enumerate the new operation and its rejected attempts as the other operations are enumerated. Verify the project with its full gate: model checks, proofs, successful and refused conformance attempts, and meaningful witnesses covering own-run failure followed by a rebuild and a subsequent build outcome. Check that the new action is unavailable to CI failures and unauthorized actors, and that all existing authority, ratification, stop-limit and merge protections still hold. Keep the project's README accurate; this prerequisite alone does not change the watcher's advertised retry behavior.

This rests on D-0045 and D-0064 (the watcher takes only protocol steps), D-0082 and D-0090 (check accepted and refused operations), D-0105 (plumbing uses tested code around proved rules), and D-0122 (current documentation). Before changing the covered decisions, inspect their dependents. A new decision must record the additional rebuild transition through the decision tooling, and the amendment must be ratified before any pinned statement or lock changes. Keep root SPEC.md and README accurate at this prerequisite too: if a changed description of the model lies outside the project build scope, whoever merges updates it before moving on, citing the supporting decisions as D-0122 requires. User-visible retry instructions change only when the final plumbing issue connects the new operation.

issues.title: Recover retries that replace failed draft pull requests
issues.body:
Issue #263 requires a retry after a failed plumbing build to run a new build of the same ratified plan, close the failed draft pull request and open a replacement. The preceding protocol amendment permits the rebuild transition. The recovery core also needs an amendment: factory/recovery currently pins OnePullRequest as at most one PR ever opened for the ratification, permits its modeled retry only when no PR exists, and has no effect for retiring a failed draft. The watcher must not evade those rules by hiding the predecessor and presenting a fresh build. This issue supplies recovery permissions and guarantees; the next plumbing issue connects them to GitHub.

Project: factory/recovery

Model an explicitly authorized rebuild attempt whose predecessor is a failed, unmerged draft. The issue protocol still decides whether a retry is allowed; recovery governs its effects. The new attempt keeps the original ratification, has its own durable identity and recorded agent run, retires the predecessor, publishes its result and answers the retry without duplicating effects. Represent enough shared, durable progress to distinguish an intended replacement from an unrelated external close after a crash. Persist the replacement intent and predecessor identity before closing the draft, and close the predecessor before opening a successor. The successor may be ready when the new build passes its checks and review, or another failed draft otherwise. A stopped run without a result is reported and requires another explicit retry; recovery never silently starts that run again. Retain the replacement intent, predecessor identity and retirement status through that stopped outcome, so a later explicit retry continues the chain even if the predecessor is already closed. Keep the current attempt's active PR/head empty when it produced no successor, as the protocol requires. The retry acknowledgement and the eventual build-result post are separate events: only the acknowledgement answers the command.

Amend the one-PR rule to allow an authorized chain of replacement attempts while permitting at most one active PR for the ratified work and at most one successor PR for each attempt. Preserve at-most-once answers and agent runs per command or attempt, lease ownership for every effect, and at-most-once merges. A replacement uses its own CI evidence; an old draft or old gate pass cannot authorize merging the successor. A predecessor found merged must not be replaced. Crashes, ambiguous effect responses and another watcher must recover the same attempt, adopt a successor already created for it, and never create an extra PR or run. Discover an already-created successor by durable attempt identity across open, closed and merged PRs, including after an ambiguous create response; a later close or merge must never cause a second successor for that attempt. Distinct later writer retries must remain possible after another failed attempt. Keep existing draft, ratification, build, stopped-build retry, note and merge paths available. A CI retry that merely watches again needs no replacement effects.

Amend the pinned statements through the modeled proposal and ratification workflow; update the model, Go core/contracts, explorer and project README. Preserve compatible existing core entry points so this prerequisite can merge before the watcher integration. Prove the changed safety guarantees and check liveness under stated fairness: an authorized retry eventually receives its answer, including stopped-run reporting, and the current successor's successful gate is eventually settled when the protocol permits it. Exercise crashes before and after recording intent, retiring the predecessor, starting and finishing the run, publishing the successor and posting the result, with lease loss and a second watcher. Include a witness that actually replaces an already-published failed draft and meaningful bug checks against duplicate replacement or unleased effects. Run the full recovery verification gate, including refused-operation conformance.

This rests on D-0064 (protocol authority), D-0069 (proved crash recovery), D-0071 (liveness and fairness), D-0072 (leases), D-0073 (durable run records and idempotent effects), D-0074 (every effect is checked against recovery), D-0082 and D-0090 (attempt coverage), and D-0122 (current documentation). Inspect decision dependents and record the changed replacement guarantee through decision tooling; it changes the pinned one-PR rule and requires a ratified modeled amendment. Keep root SPEC.md and README accurate at this prerequisite too, particularly the claim that recovery leaves closed PRs out. If such a change lies outside the project build scope, whoever merges updates it before moving on, citing the supporting decisions as D-0122 requires. User-visible retry instructions change only when the plumbing integration makes replacement available.

issues.title: Rebuild failed plumbing drafts and explain each retry
issues.body:
Finish issue #263 using the protocol and recovery amendments merged by the preceding two issues. Today a failed plumbing build leaves a draft PR and promises that retry will build again, but internal/factory/factory.go chooses only by whether the marker names a PR and watches that failed draft again. A writer's retry after an agent error, failed tests or a review asking for changes must instead build the same ratified plan again and replace its failed draft. A retry after CI's gate fails must continue watching the same PR, without starting a builder or rerunning GitHub Actions.

Kind: plumbing

Select the action from the recorded failure origin and kind of work. Published plumbing results that failed in the factory's own run use FailGate; stopped builds without a PR retain the existing rebuild path. Preserve the existing fallback for old failure markers without an explicit reason: a marker naming a PR is treated as a CI/watch failure. Keep watching for FailCI, FailUnmergeable, FailTrusted and FailMerge, and keep modeled-project retries unchanged. Draft status alone is not evidence of a failed plumbing run. A final agent error after any configured fallback must count as a failed build even when it returns partial work; tests passing alone or a missing/negative review cannot make that attempt successful.

Use the new modeled rebuild operation with a faithful source view, then the recovery operations for replacement. Keep the original plan hash, ratification and pinned acceptance tests, file scope and selected coding agent. Do not draft or ratify again. Each accepted retry gets a fresh build attempt and durable run identity; the failed attempt's saved result must not satisfy it. Preserve the failed work for inspection, close the predecessor draft without merging it, and create a distinct replacement PR from the new attempt's result. If reusing its branch, close the predecessor before pushing replacement code so its failed contents remain inspectable; a separate attempt branch is also valid. The replacement is ready only after the factory's checks and review pass; another failure remains a draft and offers the same retry behavior. Success still requires CI on the replacement's current head, the ratified plan and scope checks, and human merging of the trusted base. Identify the predecessor and successor in the issue's account of the retry.

Connect all necessary factory, run-record, repository and GitHub operations, including an idempotent, lease-checked PR close. Recovery must reconstruct the authorized replacement from shared records after a restart, including a crash after closure but before its final post. The early closed-PR observation in the factory must not misclassify its own in-progress replacement as an external close and discard the pending retry. Retain predecessor identity and retirement progress through stopped attempts with no publishable result, so a later explicit retry cannot lose the replacement or mistake an already-retired predecessor for a fresh failure. Adopt a successor already created for the same attempt without another agent run or PR, finding it by stable attempt identity even if it has since closed or merged; never adopt the predecessor as the new result merely because it shares the branch. Respect externally merged or closed PRs observed before replacement begins, and preserve their existing lifecycle handling.

Make every relevant post and card describe the chosen action. Update the local build-failure post, retry acknowledgement and refused-revise advice; the latter must not promise a build for a CI retry. In the public dashboard and /act, make the failure explanation, action label, confirmation, immediate posted-command feedback and timeline distinguish rebuilding the ratified plan and replacing draft #N from watching PR #N again. Include stopped builds without PRs and scope, merge and trusted-base failures. The server's action eligibility remains authoritative: an open failed draft still offers retry rather than revise, and changing the plan still requires closing it before revising. Rewatch text must preserve the human-only trusted-base merge rule and must not claim that retry reruns CI. Keep the command itself /invariant retry and preserve authorization checks.

Acceptance must exercise the real factory polling and publication paths with controlled builders and GitHub/repository fakes: separately cover an agent error with saved partial work, failed tests, and a review asking for changes, each leaving an open draft and each retry invoking a new build, preserving the ratified plan/tests/agent, closing the old draft and publishing exactly one distinct successor. Also test the real plumbing.Builder with a controlled backend that returns partial work and a final error while checks and review would otherwise pass: preserve and publish its work as a failed draft, then rebuild on retry. This must exercise propagation of the agent failure through the build result, not only a failing factory fake. Cover a second failed attempt and another explicit retry. Pair these with a CI-failure case that preserves PR identity, never invokes the builder or replacement operations, and continues checking the current head. Include stopped/no-result and legacy-marker compatibility, unchanged modeled-project and other rewatch paths, and rejection of unauthorized commands. Check all relevant post and card wording against those actual outcomes, including public and /act rendering, confirmation and queued feedback. Add crash/restart and lease-loss coverage around the replacement effects, showing no lost retry, duplicate answer, duplicate run, duplicate successor or merge of the retired draft. Test the GitHub close operation's request and errors and retain all existing CI/head/scope/ratification/trusted-base protections. Each new acceptance test must fail on the base used for this plumbing issue; combine unchanged behavior checks with the new distinction where needed.

Update root SPEC.md and README.md in this same change: the retry command's build-versus-watch behavior, replacement and recovery guarantees, and dashboard guidance must match the implementation. Cite the decisions supporting every changed SPEC bullet. This work rests on D-0047 (CI retry), D-0064 (protocol), D-0069/D-0072/D-0073/D-0074 (recovery), D-0105/D-0107/D-0108/D-0109 (ratified plumbing, tests, review and trusted-base merging), D-0130 (the proposal's selected agent), D-0156 (cards offer only commands the factory takes), D-0122 (documentation), and the decisions recorded for the two preceding modeled amendments. Inspect their dependents before changing what they cover. Any remaining decision about the user-visible rebuild/replacement behavior must be recorded through decision tooling by whoever merges this plumbing change, since its build cannot write decisions/.

usage.summary: Wrote [issues.json](issues.json) with three ordered issues: protocol amendment, recovery amendment, then plumbing with acceptance coverage, dashboard wording, and documentation updates. The check passed; `repo/` remains unchanged.
